newsitem.title: UK: U.S.Brooklyn Union buys into N.Irish natural gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S.Brooklyn Union buys into N.Irish natural gas.

text.p: The Brooklyn Union Gas Company of New York is to acquire a 24.5 percent interest in two British Gas Plc subsidiaries developing a natural gas industry in Northern Ireland, the U.S. and British firms said on Tuesday.
Brooklyn Union's subsidiary KeySpan International Ltd will acquire a stake in Phoenix Natural Gas Ltd and Premier Transco Ltd, a joint statement from Brooklyn Union and BG Plc said.
Details of the acquisition costs were not disclosed.

"We are delighted that a company of Brookly Union's international stature is joining us in the development of Northern Ireland's natural gas industry," said David Varney, chief executive of BG plc, formerly British Gas plc.
Robert Catell, chairman and chief executive officer of Brooklyn Union said the joint venture fitted perfectly with his company's long-term investment plans.
"We believe natural gas will be the fuel of the future for Northern Ireland," Catell said.

Phoenix Natural Gas, which has already announced plans for a 160 million sterling investment in Northern Ireland, was awarded a license to develop a natural gas industry in the British province last year.
Supplies to its first industrial customber began last December. It will also supply domestic customers.

The gas comes along a 135-km undersea pipeline from Twynholm near Kirkcudbright in southwest Scotland to the BG-owned Premier Power Station near Larne, where it supplies the power station and meets a 26-km Phoenix pipepline to Torytown near Belfast. Premier Transco completed the pipeline in August 1996 ahead of schedule after a 4.5 year planning and construction programme.
The announcement was made at a press conference held in Belfast attended by senior officials from both companies.
A BG plc spokesman declined to say how much the acquisition cost. "We are not able to go into details of the financial arrangements," he told Reuters.
"There is a possibility of further discussions with other potential joint venture partner. Clearly we would not wish to compromise our negotiating position."

BG plc comkprises the Transco gas transportation and storage business in Britain, Bg Exploration & Production, Bg International Downstream, and research and technology, pipeline inspection and property businesses.
International Downstream is involved in gas transmission and disbribution, and power generation.
